key_insight: DiaLLM shows that language models can often understand dialectal English better than they can generate it, revealing a clear robustness-generation gap. The paper’s controlled adaptation setup helps pinpoint which training and alignment choices improve dialectal output.
problem_solved: It addresses the mismatch between dialect understanding and dialect generation in large language models, especially their tendency to produce standard, US-leaning English instead of authentic dialectal varieties.
method: Continually pretrains three open-weight language model families on the International Corpus of English.
Compares implicit and explicit post-training paradigms for dialect adaptation.
Combines each post-training approach with three different model alignment strategies in a controlled experimental setup.
impact: This work gives AI/ML practitioners a clearer way to evaluate and improve dialect adaptation beyond simple comprehension benchmarks. It can help build more inclusive language models that generate text closer to real-world English varieties.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing continual pretraining, post-training, and alignment stages
Side-by-side comparison chart of dialect understanding vs. dialect generation
Matrix or heatmap of model families, adaptation methods, and alignment strategies
Icon set representing different English dialects and output styles
paper_title: DiaLLM: An Investigation into the Robustness-Generation Gap in English Dialect Adaptation
paper_authors: Jordan Painter, Dipankar Srirag, Adarsh Kappiyath, Diptesh Kanojia, Aditya Joshi
